newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Mining pays penalty tax.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Mining pays penalty tax.

text.p: Mitsui Mining Co Ltd said on Wednesday it had paid a 1.5 billion yen penalty to Japanese tax authorities who claimed that 2.6 billion yen in spending in the four years to March 31, 1995 was not tax deductable.
Despite the payment, Mitsui Mining filed a complaint with the tax authorities in September, a company spokesman said, objecting to the classification of the money.
The spending included about 2.2 billion yen paid to an oil dealer in western Japan that is now the subject of a civil lawsuit between Mitsui and Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd.
Mitsui said it was part of a brokerage fee paid to the dealer but the tax authorities said the money was used for entertainment and thus not tax deductable.

Mitsui Mining said in an affidavit last week that Mitsubishi Oil had asked it to cooperate in a scheme in which Mitsui secretly provided money to the western Japan oil dealer in financial trouble through bogus oil deals.
It says that Mitsubishi Oil guaranteed that it would later reimburse Mitsui Mining for the losses in the transactions with the dealer.
Mitsubishi Oil denied that it had been involved in any funnelling of money to the dealer.
